opening_message:
Ticket 1: Casey Wu (employee ID E005) requests write access to Source Code.

Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E005.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: write
  - comment: Casey Wu (E005) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Source Code is owned by the Engineer role, so admin is not permitted; write is the maximum for this employee. Requested write is within policy, recommending write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Source Code: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Casey Wu (E005) is a contractor with basic security training. Contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. Since training is basic, the maximum is read. Requested write exceeds the maximum, so recommending read.
reason: The two notes conflict on employment type: HR lists E005 as full-time, while the Security DB lists E005 as a contractor with only basic security training. For access decisions, the Security record is authoritative on employment classification and training: contractors may have read, or write only with advanced training. With basic training, the maximum allowed level is read. The requested write exceeds that maximum, so I grant the maximum permitted level of read.
